text:
Sam G: Hey team — running the ACME POC and we're getting logs in Splunk but no trace_id on any spans. Logs show request_id only. Any quick checks?
Maria S: Do you mean the x-trace-id header is missing in the drain events or the proxy is dropping it?
Sam G: Looks like it's missing before the drain. Splunk events have request_id: abc123 but no trace_id field. We ingest via our onprem forwarder -> redwood dedicated pool -> splunk HEC.
Kevin (ops): Common issue: upstream proxy (nginx/envoy) strips custom headers unless explicitly forwarded. Can you paste the curl you used, or an example request?
Sam G: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redwood-key>" -H "x-trace-id: 2026-03-21T15:12:34Z-abc" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
Maria S: Good — that header should get through. Do you have any edge LB or WAF that might normalise headers? Also what runtime are you hitting (hosted vs dedicated)?
Sam G: Dedicated pool in us-west-2, behind customer's AWS ALB + nginx. ALB shows 200, nginx logs show X-Trace-Id missing.
Kevin (ops): Ok sounds like nginx config. Quick patch: in the proxy block add: 

    # preserve upstream request id as X-Trace-Id
    proxy_set_header X-Trace-Id $request_id;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;

Put that in the location / proxy section and reload.
Maria S: Another thing: our onprem splunk forwarder will map trace fields only if the header key matches the parser. Some customers have parsers expecting "trace_id" not "x-trace-id". If nginx can't preserve the header name, you can inject into the body or map header to field in the forwarder config.
Anya (sales): Customer is fine with small infra changes. They asked if this affects throughput.
Kevin (ops): Minimal. This is just header passthrough. The only perf hit is a config reload. Also watch for 429s on the drain — I saw a couple of 429s earlier in the container logs, might indicate our drain endpoint is being throttled.
Sam G: I do see repeated 429s in the redwood-forwarder container last night. snippet: 

    2026-03-20T23:11:02Z forwarder ERROR http 429 splunk.hec host=hec.acme.com rate_limit

Could that cause missing KV cache entries and break trace correlation?
Kevin (ops): If events are dropped you won't get the linked span/trace events. Also, some SDKs attach trace context as KV cache keys and if KV cache misses you just have request_id. Two parallel workstreams: 1) patch nginx to forward header, 2) investigate forwarder 429s (rate limiting or HEC tokens).
Maria S: For test validation, after nginx patch, run this curl and check the redwood request logs for header echo: 

    curl -H "x-trace-id: test-TRACE-001" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -s | jq .

We also have a quick debug endpoint for POCs: https://docs.redwood.ai/poc-debug#header-echo (useful to confirm header reachability).
Sam G: Will try now. Patching nginx live.
Kevin (ops): If you can't restart nginx, as a temporary workaround you can add this transform in the forwarder pipeline to extract request_id and synthesize trace_id: 

    transforms:
      - name: synth-trace
        type: lua
        script: |
          function process(event)
            if not event.trace_id and event.request_id then
              event.trace_id = event.request_id
            end
            return event
          end

Not ideal but will let you correlate while we fix the root cause.
Anya (sales): Customer asked whether we need extra permissions to edit nginx. They have a change window at 18:00 PST. Is that soon enough?
Maria S: Yes that's fine. We should also validate that the dedicated pool doesn't have an intermediary (e.g., sidecar) removing headers. Check the pod spec for any env var like STRIP_HEADERS=true.
Sam G: Deployed nginx patch at 18:05. Running curl -> debug endpoint: header_echo shows test-TRACE-001 present. :thumbsup:
Kevin (ops): Nice. Now check Splunk for events containing test-TRACE-001. If still missing, it's either HEC mapping or forwarder dropping.
Sam G: Tail of forwarder logs now shows HTTP 200s and I see events hitting HEC. Searching Splunk for "test-TRACE-001"... found matches under index=acme traces. Trace id now appears as trace_id field. Yay.
Maria S: Great — sounds resolved. What's the plan to prevent recurrence?
Kevin (ops): I'll add a small check to our POC runbook: confirm header passthrough from LB -> nginx -> forwarder and monitor forwarder 429s (alert when >5/min). Also will add header mapping test to CI that hits the debug endpoint and asserts the header shows up in Splunk index.
Anya (sales): I'll update the deal notes (customer happy). Any pricing impact from extra forwarder throughput?
Sam G: Slight bump if they want retention, but nothing blocking the POC.
Maria S: Closing loop: deploy-bot: release/pocexport-nginx-config rolled at 2026-03-21T18:05Z
deploy-bot: build 2026.3.21-778 deployed to prod-dedicated/us-west-2
Sam G: Confirmed — logs + traces good. Closing thread. Thanks all :raised_hands:"
